definition: Cell death is the process by which a cell stops living, through several biologically distinct forms such as programmed self-destruction or injury-related death. It is a normal part of development and tissue balance, helping control cell numbers, remove abnormal cells, and shape body structures, but abnormal regulation can contribute to disease.
